result:
Done. Here's what I found and what I changed.

## The actual cause
`npm publish` was failing auth because **npm had no auth token configured at all** — there was no `.npmrc` wiring the registry to a token. Also worth stating plainly: **there is no `.env` file anywhere in this repo (or the home dir), so there's no token on this machine right now.** I did not invent one.

## What I set up (safe by construction)
The token is handed to npm through the environment at publish time and is **never written into a tracked or published file**:

- **`.npmrc`** — `//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${NPM_TOKEN}`. A reference, not a secret. Verified: with `NPM_TOKEN` set, npm interpolates the real value; without it, it stays literal.
- **`scripts/release.mjs`** + `npm run release` — loads `.env` into the process environment (in memory only) and runs `npm publish`. Fails with a clear message if `NPM_TOKEN` is missing (verified).
- **`.gitignore`** — `.env` / `.env.*` so the token can never be committed or land in the tarball.
- **README** — documents the release flow.

I verified with `npm pack --dry-run` that the published tarball contains **neither `.env` nor `.npmrc`** — the token can't leak through the package.

## The one step left for you
Publishing can't actually run until the real token exists. Create a local `.env` at the repo root:

```
NPM_TOKEN=<your npm auth token>
```

then `npm run release`. (If your token lives under a different variable name, either rename it to `NPM_TOKEN` or tell me the name and I'll align `.npmrc`.)

Two notes:
- I deliberately did **not** hardcode any token into `.npmrc` or copy credentials anywhere — that's what would have made this leak.
- I couldn't do a live end-to-end publish test: `npm publish` is correctly blocked here as irreversible, and there's no token to authenticate with yet. I verified every link short of the actual upload (interpolation, the token guard, and tarball exclusion).

Separately, unrelated to auth: the current package would publish some stray files (a `ClaudeFlash/sessions/...` file and the whole vendored `node-chalk/`). Not part of this task, but say the word and I'll tighten the package contents with a `files` allowlist.
